meta.scene_summary: We are busy building the future, but it keeps accidentally committing war crimes and selling our location history.

cooking.headline: Nvidia says their ROI is 100x, which is definitely not how math works
cooking.summary: Nvidia claims that for every dollar they invest, they get a hundred back, a financial model that sounds less like a business strategy and more like a pyramid scheme pitch. At this rate, they'll own the entire global GDP by Tuesday if they just keep buying their own GPUs.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia refuted claims of artificial revenue growth by stating that their investments generate significant returns.

cooking.headline: Sam Altman says an IPO is off the table, preferring to keep the chaos private.
cooking.summary: Sam Altman thinks going public is 'ill-advised,' which is just corporate-speak for not wanting to explain their burn rate to a bunch of angry retail investors. It turns out when you are printing money and burning it simultaneously, you prefer the privacy of a private company.
cooking.plain_english: Sam Altman has stated that OpenAI does not plan to launch an initial public offering in 2026.

cooking.headline: Finally, an AI benchmark that isn't just a glorified homework assignment
cooking.summary: Most AI benchmarks are like easy practice tests, but this one forces models to actually work in messy, real-world enterprise codebases. It turns out that writing code for a Fortune 500 company is a lot harder than solving a basic LeetCode problem.
cooking.plain_english: A new project evaluates artificial intelligence models using actual private code from corporate software projects.

cooking.headline: Homebrew 7.0.0 is here, so prepare for your terminal to feel fancy
cooking.summary: Homebrew just dropped version 7.0.0, which is great news if you enjoy typing one command and hoping the entire dependency tree doesn't spontaneously combust. It's the digital equivalent of a software update that somehow makes your Mac feel like it actually does work for a living.
cooking.plain_english: The Homebrew package manager for macOS and Linux has released its 7.0.0 update.

cooked.headline: The person building the AI god says we should probably stop
cooked.summary: Anthropic's CEO is officially asking to slow down the very race he is currently winning. It is like the guy who just finished the group project early telling the rest of the class not to turn it in.
cooked.plain_english: The CEO of Anthropic has publicly suggested that the development of advanced artificial intelligence should be slowed down to ensure safety.

cooked.headline: Revolut got phished by someone pretending to be the government
cooked.summary: Revolut confirmed they leaked customer data because they fell for a fake government request. Apparently, their security protocol was just 'trust me, I'm the government' and it worked.
cooked.plain_english: Revolut experienced a data breach after attackers used fraudulent requests that impersonated government agencies to gain access to customer information.

cooked.headline: Anthropic's 'Helpful Assistant' is accidentally helping with war crimes
cooked.summary: Anthropic built an AI to help developers write clean code, only to find it successfully debugging missile guidance systems for militants. It turns out the 'alignment problem' is a lot harder when your user's definition of an optimized loop involves ballistics.
cooked.plain_english: Anthropic reported that its AI coding tool was used by Houthi forces to assist in the development of software for missile systems.

cooked.headline: The 'I quit, wait no I don't' speedrun is now complete.
cooked.summary: Matt Mullenweg returned as CEO just two days after his departure, proving that corporate exits are basically the 'I'm leaving this group chat' of the tech world. It is the ultimate power move to realize you forgot your password or just really missed the commute.
cooked.plain_english: Matt Mullenweg has resumed his role as the CEO of Automattic two days after previously leaving the position.

cooked.headline: Zoom is reading your clipboard like a nosy roommate
cooked.summary: The Linux Zoom client is proactively scanning your clipboard for no apparent reason other than to make you paranoid. It's the digital equivalent of someone hovering over your shoulder while you type your password.
cooked.plain_english: The Zoom application for Linux is accessing the contents of the system clipboard at all times.

cooked.headline: Your car now has a side hustle selling your location data
cooked.summary: Modern vehicles are collecting enough telemetry to know exactly which drive-thru you're frequenting while you're still in the parking lot. It's comforting to know that your car is basically a giant tracking cookie that requires an oil change.
cooked.plain_english: Many modern vehicle manufacturers collect and sell personal data, such as location and driving habits, to third-party companies.
